\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Indicator Regularity}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.IndicatorRegularity
\section{Overview}
At nonzero noise scale, averaged indicators have a product Gaussian density representation. Differentiation of this density gives global bounds and Lipschitz regularity for their ordinary derivatives.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Density representation of averaged indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_integral_density}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_affine_gaussian_pi_eq_density}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, then for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\prod_i p_{\sin^2u}(\cos u\,x_i,z_i)1_A(z)\,dz$, where $p_v(c,z)$ is the $N(c,v)$ density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cosine scaling is a contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_cosineScaling_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $n\ge0$ and $u\in\mathbb R$, the linear map $x\mapsto\cos u\,x$ on $\mathbb R^n$ has operator norm at most one for the maximum norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of an averaged indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_integral_density,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_integral_gaussianProductDensity}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, $u_u$ is differentiable at every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, with $D u_u(x)[h]=\cos u\int1_A(z)\,\partial_c[\prod_i p_{\sin^2u}(c_i,z_i)]_{c=\cos u\,x}[h]\,dz$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density and $\partial_c$ is differentiation in the mean vector.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform averaged-indicator derivative bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_fderiv_averagedGaussianIndicator_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_cosineScaling_le_one,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_smul_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, then $\|D u_u(x)\|\le n(1+1/\sin^2u)$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, with operator norm for the maximum norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Pullback through a linear contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_comp_contraction}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a real normed vector space, $D:E\to\mathcal L(E,\mathbb R)$ be $C$-Lipschitz in operator norm with $C\ge0$, and $L:E\to E$ be continuous linear with $\|L\|\le1$. Then $x\mapsto D(Lx)\circ L$ is $C$-Lipschitz.
\end{lemma}

If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, then $x\mapsto D u_u(x)$ is globally $2n^2/\sin^2u$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^n$.
